title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator Protection skill warns of suspected social engineering
summary: Hold: the controls table says automation is not documented, although Microsoft publishes a PowerShell reference for managing Teams app state. That reference has conflicting blocking examples, which justifies withholding a blocking command but not reporting that documentation does not exist. The briefing otherwise accurately distinguishes the tenant notice's rollout window from the roadmap target and qualifies the Protection-specific unknowns.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Facilitator can be allowed or blocked in Teams admin center under Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Facilitator app availability control can govern availability for the entire organisation.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control whether Facilitator is available to your entire organization or to a certain group of users.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: API and automation cell
claims.claim: An automation surface for controlling the Facilitator app's availability and state is not yet documented.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.
claims.fix: Do not render the automation cell as 'Not yet documented'. Replace that cell's absence statement with 'Microsoft documents Update-M365TeamsApp for app-state management, but its examples describe both -IsBlocked $true and -IsBlocked $false as unblocking. Use the documented admin UI; no blocking command is provided here.' Link it to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp and retain the existing caution rather than inventing a Boolean mapping.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: control note
claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking an app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: control note
claims.claim: The cited reference does not establish a reliable blocking call because its examples conflict on the meaning of -IsBlocked.
claims.quote: Example 3: -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app. Example 4: -IsBlocked $false ... Unblocks 1Page App
